resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Occupancy (resale inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Beach Haven Zoning Department (Construction and Zoning)
resale_co.lead_time: Allow 2 weeks to schedule the inspection; resale inspections are done Tuesday and Thursday afternoons
requirements: Visual inspection only, not a structural inspection
General condition of the lot, exterior and interior
Porch, deck and stair condition
Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarm(s)
Acceptable electrical and plumbing systems
Proper venting of heating equipment
Relief valves on water heaters and boilers piped down to within 6 inches of the floor (no plastic or galvanized pipe); water heater cabinets open for the inspection
Proper fire separation between an attached garage and living areas
Bedroom windows open easily for escape
House numbers on the building (3 inch numbers for homes)
Door locks on exit doors work and are not double-keyed
Portable fire extinguisher (2A:10B:C, no more than 10 lbs) mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen and no more than 5 feet above the floor (still listed on the Borough's 2024 sheet)
Current plot plan survey and flood elevation certificate with raised seals in the buyer's name
No open permits: all open permits must be finaled before the resale inspection
Property must be unoccupied, alarm systems disabled and dogs removed or crated at the inspection

fees.label: Resale Certificate of Occupancy, each residential unit
fees.quote: Resale Certificate of Occupancy Each Residential Unit $75.00

resale_co.how_to_apply: Bring the completed Resale Certificate of Occupancy form, the other listed paperwork (current plot plan and elevation certificate, filed deed restriction, condominium certification if a condo), a check made out to the Borough of Beach Haven and property access information to the Construction and Zoning office, 300 Engleside Avenue (the form also lists cash). The deed restriction must be filed with the Ocean County Clerk's Office in Toms River.

resale_co.notes: Fees are on the Construction and Zoning page fee table (each residential unit $75.00, each commercial unit $150.00, reinspection $20.00) and on the 2023 Resale Certificate of Occupancy form (single $75.00, duplex $150.00, commercial $150.00, re-inspect $20.00). The Borough's 2024 resale requirements sheet still requires a mounted portable fire extinguisher; the state dropped the extinguisher from the state sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19), but this is the Borough's own resale checklist, so confirm with the office. Resident Emergency Access Placards (all non-condo owners) must be present and visible at the inspection and left for the new owner. Rental properties are separate: landlord registration with the Borough and a Borough fire inspection for each seasonal year or long-term tenant change. Re-checked 2026-10-13: the Construction and Zoning page (last updated 2026-09-14), its fee table and the resale forms are unchanged.

requirements: Borough certificate of smoke alarm and carbon monoxide alarm compliance (CSACMAPFEC) on the sale of any property (Borough Code Chapter 95, Article XIV, adopted July 13, 2026)
Smoke alarms on every living level including the basement, and within 10 feet of bedrooms on levels with bedrooms
All smoke alarms, including hardwired, must be under 10 years old

Homes built before 1978: at least one 10-year sealed battery smoke alarm on each level; 1978 to 1983: hardwired alarms on each level; 1984 to 1990: interconnected hardwired alarms with battery backup on each level; 1991 and later: also in every bedroom
Hardwired alarms that need replacing must be replaced with hardwired alarms, not battery alarms

Carbon monoxide alarm in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas if the home has a fuel-burning device or an attached garage; battery and plug-in CO alarms should be under 5 years old, combination smoke/CO alarms under 10
Portable fire extinguishers are no longer required (as of February 3, 2025)
Do not mount alarms in unfinished attics, garages, stairwells, the top of basement stairs or kitchens

fire_cert.notes: Changed since the last check: the Borough of Beach Haven now issues the resale smoke/CO certificate itself. Ordinance 2026-10C (introduced June 8, 2026, finally adopted July 13, 2026) replaced Borough Code Chapter 95, Article XIV: all properties must be inspected for CSACMAPFEC compliance on sale, certificates issued by the Borough are required and are not transferable, and the fee for a sale is $35 when the application reaches the Borough more than 10 working days before settlement, with $35 for the third and each later reinspection. The Ocean County Fire Marshal's Resale and Rental Home Inspections page no longer lists Beach Haven among the towns it inspects (its list now has Barnegat Light, Bay Head, Harvey Cedars, Long Beach Twp., Point Pleasant Boro., Ship Bottom and South Toms River), so the county fees ($45/$90/$161) recorded before no longer apply. The NJ DCA LEA registry (July 2026) still shows the county (code C) as Beach Haven's fire code enforcing agency and the state directory lists 'Beach Haven Boro' under smoke detector compliance. The Borough has not posted fees for applications made 10 or fewer working days before settlement, a named fire inspector, an email or an application form; the Construction and Zoning page still says the online scheduling link is 'COMING SOON'. The Borough's Inspection Information Sheet (September 2, 2026) lists the alarm rules and says portable fire extinguishers are no longer required. The Borough's own resale certificate of occupancy inspection (Zoning Department) also checks smoke and CO alarms.

other_items.detail: All open permits must be finaled before the resale inspection.

other_items.label: Condominium certification
other_items.detail: Condo units use the Borough's Condominium Certification form listed with the resale paperwork.

other_items.label: Emergency access placard

open_questions: How does a seller apply for and schedule the Borough smoke/CO (CSACMAPFEC) inspection while the online link is 'coming soon', and who is the Borough Fire Inspector?
What does the Borough charge for smoke/CO applications received 10 or fewer working days before settlement? Only the $35 fee for more than 10 working days is published.
Is the $35 smoke/CO fee separate from the $75 resale certificate of occupancy fee, and can both inspections be done in one visit?

Does the Borough still require the mounted portable fire extinguisher on its resale CO checklist (2024 sheet) after P.L.2025, c.19? Its September 2026 smoke/CO sheet says extinguishers are no longer required.
How long is the Resale Certificate of Occupancy valid?
